## Observation
On an S3 ticket store (git-remote-s3 0.4.2, git 2.56.0), every reconciler pass whose lock remote is the S3 store fails at ref-lock acquisition. `_push_cas` (src/rebar/reconciler/_ref_lock.py:733) pushes `<blob-oid>:<ref>` with --force-with-lease; git-remote-s3 passes the source side to `git bundle create`, which refuses a bare object id ("Refusing to create empty bundle", exit 128). Rebar sees only "fatal: unknown error" because the helper swallows git's message. The same push to a plain bare remote succeeds. Reproduced against moto and a real scratch bucket (since deleted); evidence: .rebar/worktrees/inv-s3-reflock/.rebar/scratch/inv-76869/.

Intent: commit a06d00a / ADR 0031 (ticket 524d-00fa-66ef-4432) designed the lock as a bare-ref CAS proven only on GitHub and a local remote. ADR 0093 and docs/s3-backend.md later state reconcile "works identically" on S3 without a test.

On real S3 through the helper: a temporary named ref gives single-winner create; blob-to-blob renew/steal is always rejected (fast-forward only unless `+`, and `+` drops the lease); a commit chain whose parent is the observed lock gives single-winner renew/steal; delete has no lock or compare, so a release racing a steal both succeeded in 2 of 10 rounds.

Related, found in the same investigation:
- The PUSH_PENDING hint says "check connectivity to origin" when the remote is not origin.
- Two checkouts sharing one tracker can name different sync remotes (ADP: main checkout defaults to origin/GitHub, PR worktree uses s3tickets) with no warning.
- The same blob-plus-lease push also writes `refs/reconciler/gate` (set_gate, set_pause), `refs/reconciler/last-pass` (last_pass.publish via `_cas_advance`), and deletes the gate on clear/resume and repair-pause cleanup, so all of them fail or race on S3 the same way.

Verified for this plan: git-remote-s3 0.4.2 `cmd_push` (remote.py) rejects a non-forced push whose remote tip is not an ancestor, then takes a per-ref S3 conditional-write lock and re-lists the ref, rejecting with "stale remote" if it changed; GitHub and local remotes reject a non-fast-forward push natively. Losers on S3 also see PreconditionFailed, ConditionalRequestConflict, or a 404 HeadObject as the rejection text. `_read_blob_bytes` already reads a commit-shaped ref (`<ref>:lock.json` / `gate.json`). rebar 0.13.x readers: an unrecognised gate mode is treated as no gate; a lock blob with extra fields decodes; a corrupt or unreadable lock is treated as held (fail-closed).

## Decision (operator, 2026-10-30, option 4)
One mechanism on every remote: each write to a `refs/reconciler/*` ref is a commit whose parent is the tip the writer read, pushed as a plain non-forced fast-forward from a temporary named ref. Release and clear become fast-forward marker commits instead of deletes. Prove all lock operations in a scratch bucket under the `frontier` AWS profile before landing.

## Plan
1. Chain writes (`_ref_lock_push.py`, called through `_ref_lock._cas_write`). Wrap the payload blob in a one-file tree (`gate.json` for the gate ref, `lock.json` otherwise, the existing reader convention) and a commit whose parent is the observed tip (no parent when the ref is absent), with a fixed reconciler identity and a random nonce in the message. Local (no remote): `update-ref <ref> <commit> <observed>`. Remote: create `refs/reconciler/tmp/<uuid>`, push `refs/reconciler/tmp/<uuid>:<ref>` with no `+` and no lease, delete the temp ref in `finally`. Never push a bare object id and never push a delete.
2. Outcome by re-read, not by message text. On a non-zero push, re-fetch the ref: tip equals our commit -> success; tip differs from the observed old -> CAS mismatch (another writer won); tip still equals old -> genuine failure, raised with the remote, ref and full stderr tail (replacing the 200-character truncation), so the real git or helper message reaches the operator.
3. Legacy blob tips (written by rebar <= 0.13 on git remotes): a blob cannot be a parent, so a write over an observed blob tip uses the existing `--force-with-lease` path once, pushed from the temporary named ref; afterwards the ref is a chain. An S3 remote never holds a legacy tip (those writes always failed there).
4. Markers that older readers understand. Lock release writes `lock.json` = `{holder: "", lease_secs: 1, heartbeat_ns: now, fence: <current fence + 1>, released: true}`; new readers return free, 0.13.x readers see an expired lease and steal it after one second. Gate clear writes `gate.json` = `{gated_mode: "cleared"}`; new readers return open, 0.13.x readers treat the unknown mode as no gate and no pause. `read`, `read_gate`, `read_pause_with_oid` and `clear_gate` treat both markers as absent; `acquire` reads the tip and chains onto an absent ref or a released marker, and raises RefLockHeldError on a live lock without pushing. `release` keeps its bool contract (True only when our marker landed) and still clears the local copy.
5. Callers keep their signatures: `acquire`, `renew` and `try_break_if_stale` return the new tip commit oid; `_cas_advance` keeps its bool contract for `last_pass.publish`; `_repair_pause` keeps its observed-oid release. Read `<oid>:<name>` instead of `<ref>:<name>` in `_read_blob_bytes` so a read is pinned to the oid it observed.
6. PUSH_PENDING hint in src/rebar/_commands/fsck_tracker_health.py names the configured tickets remote instead of "origin".
7. Docs: ADR 0031 amendment (chain, markers, mixed-version behaviour, break-glass now "write a released marker"; deleting a live holder's ref lets its next renew re-create it); docs/s3-backend.md and ADR 0093 state the lock and gate refs now work on S3 with the scratch-bucket evidence, warn that every checkout sharing a tracker must name the same `[sync] remote`, and record the S3 cost that each push and fetch transfers the whole chain as one bundle, with the measured size per update.
8. Tests first (local bare remotes plus a recording git shim): see acceptance criteria. Held-out tests that read the raw remote ref (tests/interfaces/facades/test_bridge_cli_heldout.py `_remote_blob`, tests/interfaces/facades/test_reconciler_last_pass_heldout.py `_remote_payload`) read blob-only today; they are changed to read the payload through the commit and to treat the released marker as free, because the remote storage format changes by decision.
9. Scratch-bucket proof under `frontier` before landing, using the real helper: 6 clones x 5 rounds each for acquire (absent and released tips), renew-vs-steal, release-vs-steal, gate set/clear, and last-pass publish; exactly one winner per round and no lost update; record per-update bundle growth over 200 updates; delete the bucket. Results go on this ticket.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every remote push from `_ref_lock` uses `refs/reconciler/tmp/<id>` as its source, never a bare oid, never `+`, and never a delete refspec.
- [ ] After acquire, renew, steal, gate set, pause set and last-pass publish, the remote ref is a commit whose first parent is the previously observed tip, or a root commit when the ref was absent.
- [ ] Two clones racing acquire on an absent ref and on a released marker produce exactly one winner; the loser gets RefLockHeldError.
- [ ] Renew racing a steal, and release racing a steal, each end with exactly one owner; the losing renew raises LeaseLostError and the losing release returns False.
- [ ] After release, `read()` returns None and a 0.13.x decoder (`_decode_blob` from v0.13.1) decodes the marker as a lease of 1 second.
- [ ] After `clear_gate`, `read_gate()` and `read_pause()` return None and the marker's mode is not a recognised Mode.
- [ ] Over a legacy blob tip on a bare remote, renew and set_gate succeed once through the lease path and leave a commit tip.
- [ ] A push rejected while the remote tip is unchanged raises with the remote's stderr in the message; a rejection after the tip moved is a CAS mismatch.
- [ ] The PUSH_PENDING line names the configured tickets remote.
- [ ] The scratch-bucket results (winners per round, bundle size per update) are recorded on this ticket and the bucket is deleted.
- [ ] ADR 0031, ADR 0093 and docs/s3-backend.md describe the chain, the markers, mixed-version behaviour, the same-sync-remote rule, and the measured S3 transfer cost.

## Non-goals
Bounding or compacting the chain (needs a forced write, which has no compare on S3); changing the S3 helper; a CI job that talks to real S3.
